classification.difficultyReason: Construct the equilateral triangle, introduce a perpendicular height and use symmetry to halve the base, then calculate the height with Pythagoras and retain it exactly for the area.

content.prompt: Draw an equilateral triangle of side length $4\text{ cm}$. Find, correct to 2 decimal places, the height of this triangle and its area.

answer.short:
Height $=3.46\text{ cm}$; area $=6.93\text{ cm}^2$ (both to 2 decimal places).

The perpendicular height bisects the base; use Pythagoras’ theorem and retain the exact height when calculating the area.
answer.worked:
Draw an equilateral triangle with each side $4\text{ cm}$. Its perpendicular height bisects the base into two lengths of $2\text{ cm}$. Let the height be $h$ cm.

$$\begin{align*}h^2+2^2&=4^2\\h^2+4&=16\\h^2&=12\\h&=\sqrt{12}\\h&\approx3.46\end{align*}$$

The height is $3.46\text{ cm}$, correct to 2 decimal places. Using the exact height:

$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\times4\times\sqrt{12}\\A&=2\sqrt{12}\\A&\approx6.93\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
